Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe p99 spikes on long-history sessions - urgent

Quick triage below (initial):
- Observed at 06:28 PT: queue depth on serving pool gpuz-13..gpuz-17 increased sharply.
- KV cache miss ratio for long-history requests (>=20k tokens) jumped from 8% -> 54% which forces recompute of earlier layers and causes long per-request GPU busy time.
- We see elevated host-side GC on warmup threads and serialization stalls in our batching layer for streams > 8k tokens.
- Error spike correlates with client streaming disconnects after 5s on some paths (likely retry + queueing).

Attachments: p99-trace.pdf (compiled distributed traces), service-logs-20261117.zip (per-host logs).

Short-term mitigations I can apply immediately:
1) Route requests with history length >16k to a lower-memory "truncation" path that drops older context (best-effort) — reduces p99 by ~60% in testing.
2) Apply tenant-level soft rate limit for concurrent long-history sessions (configurable cap of 8 concurrent >16k streams).
3) Enable prefix-only KV caching aggressively for ELR-47.

Tradeoffs: truncation affects recall for multi-session continuity; rate-limiting may increase client-side retries. Recommend customer opt-in to truncation for next 24h while we stabilize.

I'll stand by to flip these. Need permission to push tenant routing changes and rate-limit.

—Sean
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

[attachments: p99-trace.pdf, service-logs-20261117.zip]

Ken — thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the disruption. Weve done an initial triage and propose the following immediate plan to reduce customer impact:

1) Short-term (minutes): Route sessions with >16k tokens to a temporary truncation path (drops oldest context but preserves most recent 16k). This reduces p99 in our tests ~60%.
2) Short-term: Apply a soft tenant-level concurrency cap of 8 active long-history streams for Elara. This prevents queue smearing to unaffected requests.
3) Medium-term (24-72h): Team will investigate KV cache behavior and implement improved cache warm-up for long-history sessions; will follow up with a timeline.

If you agree, we will apply the two short-term mitigations now and schedule a 30-min call immediately to walk through tradeoffs and next steps. We can also offer a goodwill credit for the affected window; Rishi, please advise.

Please confirm if Elara wants automatic truncation or prefers a manual opt-in on a per-session basis.

—Monica

Subject: Executive brief: ElaraHealth long-history tail incident and next steps

Rishi — quick executive summary following yesterday's incident (ELR-47):

What happened:
- Between 06:28-11:15 PT on 2026-11-17, ElaraHealth experienced p99 regressions up to 6.8s for sessions containing ~20-28k tokens. Error rate rose to ~3.7% for streaming responses.

Immediate action taken:
- Applied tenant routing to route >16k requests to truncation path (deployed at 10:07 PT).
- Soft concurrency cap (8) for long-history streams in place until further notice.
- Enabled aggressive prefix KV caching for ELR-47.

Impact and mitigation status:
- Post-mitigation p99 dropped to ~1.9s and error rate returned to baseline. Customer agreed to temporary truncation while we deliver a permanent fix.

Root cause hypothesis (work in progress):
- Sudden increase in KV cache miss ratio for long-history requests caused recompute overhead in GPU runtime and queueing in the batching layer; likely triggered by a combination of cache eviction pressure and a recent change in the batching heuristic dealing with streaming frames.

Requests for leadership:
1) Approval to offer a one-week goodwill credit for the affected window (ELR-47).
2) Prioritize a 72-hour task force (infra + runtime + product) to deliver improved cache warm-up and a safer fallback that preserves more historical context (owners: Sean / runtime team).

Attachments: runbook-rate-limit.docx (proposed steps we executed and rollback plan).

Happy to brief you live; we have a record of the customer call notes and are drafting the executive note for Elara's CTO.

—Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
